about: Stage E1k staging (proposal; never applied by this branch). Adds a comparison band to the staged T-ENE-5 row of docs/staging/e-targets.patch.json (itself not yet in data/targets.json): a direction band for the ledger reading of mothers' reserve change by the age of the youngest infant, from emeryThompson2012's abstract. It changes no accept band. Applying it goes with the staged energy rows (integrator: protocolLog entry and new freeze). How the E1i reference B2 compares: docs/staging/e1k-prereg.md §1.3-1.4. Also proposes T-INF-6 (grooming between mothers and their own unweaned infants: stanton2014, lonsdorf2014, nishida1988), a new held-out row, staged after the model's value had been seen (flagged).

targets.definition: Energy-balance reading of mothers by time since birth: months 0-6, 6-12 and 12-24, within mothers.

field.value: C-peptide depressed for about 6 months postpartum, then a net increase through the second year; cycling resumes only after sustained gain; lower profiles in poorer foraging areas

accept.basis: months 0-6 below the mother's own later level; net rise through year 2

targets.notes: ENCODED while the C8c lactation taper is on: its knots lactTaperStartY 0.5 and lactTaperEndY 2 were set from this study. Counts as validation only if E1 derives the cost of lactation from milk energy and infant demand without those knots; set encoded to false at registration only in that case. How to measure: as T-ENE-4, grouped by the age of the youngest unweaned offspring from the census. Stage E1f: no chimpanzee source shows milk output falling in year 2 (badescu2022: nursing steady from 1 to 4 y; e-sources §14.3), so a year-2 recovery must come from the mother's own intake, not from a falling milk cost. Read the ledger's daily balance (change of reserves per day) by the age of the youngest infant; a 90-day window needs births at its start (energy-diagnose --term-births) to see months 0-6.

comparisonBand.units: % of the usable store per day (ledger truth: mean daily change of a mother's reserves ÷ her store, mothers grouped by the age of their youngest unweaned infant), mothers whose youngest infant is 0.5-2 y
comparisonBand.basis: sign only: emeryThompson2012 (abstract, 17 Kanyawara mothers, urinary C-peptide): depressed for six months postpartum, 'thereafter showing a net increase through the second year'; 'Cycling resumed only after a sustained period of energy gain'. No field size exists (C-peptide is an index; no chimpanzee calibration to kcal), so the lower edge is zero widened by the Track E design guard (0.05%/day, design). Months 0-6: negative expected, size unsourced, no band. Infants >= 2 y: same direction before cycling resumes, timing not in the abstract, no band.

revisions.reason: Line audit (docs/staging/e1k-prereg.md §1): the field reports the sign of nursing mothers' energy balance by lactation stage, not a size; a direction band on the ledger reading lets the staged row be compared with the model's reserve change. Simulated values seen when this was written: B2 (E1i 5-seed confirm) -0.083 (0.5-1 y) and -0.186 (1-2 y) %/day; the band follows the source's sign and the existing design guard only.

targets.metric: Grooming between mothers and their own unweaned infants
targets.definition: Share of a mother's daytime focal samples in which she grooms her own unweaned infant, by the infant's age class (1-2 y, 2-3 y); beside it, the share of an infant's daytime samples in which it grooms anyone, by age.

field.value: mother grooming her infant 0.027-0.029 of time at infant age 1-2 y, 0.028-0.031 at 2-3 y (firstborn and laterborn means)
field.n: mother-infant pairs well sampled in each year of the infant's life
field.method: 1-min instantaneous point samples, follows of 6-12 h

field.value: infant social grooming from 0% of time in the first six months to 3.07% at 4.5 y
field.note: values between the two ends are in Table 1 (not read)

field.value: infants under 2 y rarely groomed their mothers; older adolescents reciprocated about equally

accept.units: share of the mother's daytime (mother grooming her own infant, infant 1-3 y)
accept.basis: stanton2014's means 0.027-0.031, x 0.5 to x 2 (one site, widened; no second site found)

targets.notes: Staged by E1k, never applied. Seen when this was staged: the E1k diagnosis of the reference B2 (seeds 48 and 7, 30 + 60 days, simulation truth) had mothers of infants of 2-4 y in grooming episodes with their own infant 33.5% of daylight (the mother grooming in about 95% of that time) and infants of 2-4 y grooming their mother 24% of daylight; the band follows the field values only. How to measure: with the existing focal protocol, follow mothers with an unweaned infant and score each point as the mother grooming her own infant or not; separately score infants' own grooming.
